findings.issue: The tab name is skipped on ANY OSError for that name, and the error is not kept: _write_shapes appends only the name, so the SKIPPED line says 'this filesystem refused to create a file named' with no errno. On a filesystem where the write fails for an unrelated reason (EACCES, ENOSPC) the case would skip with a reason that is not shown to be true. The `absent` argument to _harness.skip is bool(tab_refused), which is always true inside that branch, so the skip's own grading cannot ever fire.
findings.resolution: Have _write_shapes return (name, exc) pairs, or record the errno, and put it in the skip mechanism text (for example 'refused with [Errno 22] Invalid argument'). Optionally narrow the absorbed set to the errnos Windows raises for the name. That needs a Windows run, so printing the error is the safe step.

intent.note: Clause: 'Build the tab-named fixture only where the filesystem accepts it and say so when it is skipped ... the block's other cases must still run on Windows.' The diff does this. _write_shapes writes every shape through an injected writer. An OSError on TAB_NAME only is recorded (`if name != TAB_NAME: raise`), and any other name's OSError re-raises, so a narrowed fixture cannot happen silently. Where the tab file was refused, tso3 reports it by name via _harness.skip ('tso3 ... SKIPPED HERE - this filesystem refused to create a file named ...'). The post-commit edit of the tab file is guarded by `if not tab_refused`, so tso1 and tso2 still run. tso4 and tso5 exercise the builder on every platform through a refusing writer, so the Windows branch is covered on macOS and Linux. I ran `python3 tests/test__tree_stamp.py --selftest` once: tso1 to tso5 PASS, 65/65 cases passed. The executor's outcome describes the diff accurately: the 61 to 65 case count, the import errno, the tso3, tso4 and tso5 roles, and the left-alone Windows-legal names. Dependants: _tree_stamp.py is unchanged, test_stamp_verification.py defines its own helpers, and sweep-costs.json keys by path with no stage added, so their answers hold. Caveat: block tso never got past fixture building on Windows in the CI run, so tso1 and tso2 have not been seen on Windows with the other shapes (non-ASCII name, conflict stages). The orchestrator's CI run is the verdict there.
